claim_verdicts.evidence: Transient: "created each time it's requested from the service container." Scoped: "created once per client request (connection)." Singleton: "created either: The first time they're requested. ... Every subsequent request of the service implementation from the dependency injection container uses the same instance." "singleton services are disposed when the ServiceProvider is disposed on application shutdown."

"The framework creates a scope per request, and RequestServices exposes the scoped service provider. All scoped services are valid for as long as the request is active." "In apps that process requests, scoped services are disposed at the end of the request." Docs tie disposal to the end of the request; the lesson's "closes it when the response has been sent" (§4) is more specific than anything found.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: ASP.NET Core opens a new scope for each request and disposes it when the request ends, so inside one request every class asking for a scoped type gets the same object, and the next request gets a fresh one.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "Entity Framework Core does not support multiple parallel operations being run on the same DbContext instance. This includes both parallel execution of async queries and any explicit concurrent use from multiple threads." "A DbContext instance is designed to be used for a single unit-of-work." "DbContext is Not thread-safe."

"The AddDbContext extension method registers DbContext types with a scoped lifetime by default." Same sentence in the .NET DI note: "When using Entity Framework Core, the AddDbContext extension method registers DbContext types with a scoped lifetime by default."

OrdersController.cs:12 `OrdersController(OrderService orderService, IOrderRepository repository)`; OrderService.cs:6 `OrderService(IOrderRepository repository, INotifier notifier)`; EfOrderRepository.cs:7 `EfOrderRepository(DonHangDbContext db)`. All scoped (claim 5), and scoped = "created once per client request" (claim 1) → one EfOrderRepository and one DonHangDbContext per request.

JwtTokenService.cs:11 `public sealed class JwtTokenService(IConfiguration configuration)`; :15 inside IssueToken `new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(configuration["Jwt:SigningKey"]!))`. The class declares no fields; only the captured primary-constructor parameter.

Program.cs:57-62 `using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope()) { var context = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<DonHangDbContext>(); ... }`. Docs: "The following code shows how to resolve a scoped service for a limited duration when the app starts: using (var serviceScope = app.Services.CreateScope())"; "Scoped services are disposed by the container that created them."

Transient: "created each time it's requested from the service container" → controller and OrderService each get a new EfOrderRepository. "It's also fine to: ... Resolve a scoped service from another scoped or transient service." Scoped: "created once per client request" → both repositories receive the same DonHangDbContext.

Supported, not just opinion: "Do not resolve a scoped service directly from a singleton ... Doing so causes the scoped service to behave like a singleton, which can lead to incorrect state when processing subsequent requests." EF: "When concurrent access goes undetected, it can result in undefined behavior, application crashes and data corruption."

issues.text: Unlisted claim: "would fail" is stronger than the docs. EF Core throws InvalidOperationException only when it detects concurrent use; "When concurrent access goes undetected, it can result in undefined behavior, application crashes and data corruption." (efcore dbcontext-configuration/index.md:405-407). Same wording in §6 misconception 1 ("fail when two requests query at once").
issues.quote: two queries running at once on it would fail
issues.fix: Change to "two queries running at once on it could throw an error or corrupt its state" (and in §6: "and break when two requests query at once"). Add the detection sentence to claim 3's ledger entry.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: "keeps ... a connection for one unit of work". The EF Core lifetime docs describe the unit of work as creation, tracking, SaveChanges, disposal; they do not say the context holds a connection for that span (EF opens/closes connections per operation by default). Not in the ledger.
issues.quote: A `DbContext` keeps a change tracker and a connection for one unit of work
issues.fix: Drop "and a connection": "A `DbContext` keeps a change tracker for one unit of work" (supported by dbcontext-configuration/index.md:18-32).

issues.text: "transient never" contradicts the docs on disposal tracking: "In apps that process requests, transient services are disposed at the end of the request" — the container does keep disposable transients until the scope ends. Also "how long to keep an object" for transient reads as zero lifetime.
issues.quote: singleton for the app, scoped per request, transient never
issues.fix: Rewrite line 1: "A service lifetime tells the container when to build a new object and when to hand back one it already built: singleton once for the app, scoped once per request, transient on every resolve."
